claims: Gary Woodland is the 2019 U.S. Open champion.
In March 2026, Gary Woodland revealed he has been battling PTSD.
Gary Woodland underwent brain surgery in September 2023 to remove a tumor.
Gary Woodland's PTSD followed his September 2023 brain surgery.
Gary Woodland's symptoms included severe anxiety on the course.
Gary Woodland's symptoms included fear on the course.
Gary Woodland's symptoms included panic attacks on the course.
Gary Woodland reported feeling "1,000 pounds lighter" after speaking openly about his condition.
Gary Woodland's PTSD stemmed from the trauma of his brain surgery.
Gary Woodland's PTSD stemmed from the preceding fear-driven period where he believed he was dying.
Gary Woodland described feeling hypervigilant on the course.
Gary Woodland described experiencing blurry vision on the course.
Gary Woodland described needing to hide in bathrooms to cry.
Gary Woodland was once startled by a scorer behind him, leading to anxiety.
Gary Woodland has worked with the PGA Tour to implement security protocols.
Gary Woodland is receiving support from the golf community.
Gary Woodland continued to play despite the struggles.
Gary Woodland stated, "I'm not going to let this thing win".
Shortly after opening up about his battle, Gary Woodland held the lead in the 2026 Houston Open.
